compound.name: cis-spiroether (cis-en-yn-dicycloether, (Z)-tonghaosu)
compound.one_liner: Chamomile's polyacetylene spiroether; anti-inflammatory in mouse ear tests.

identity.iupac: (Z)-2-(hexa-2,4-diyn-1-ylidene)-1,6-dioxaspiro[4.4]non-3-ene (name from the NIST WebBook entry title; not a PubChem-computed IUPAC name)
identity.note: No PubChem CID found for the cis/(Z) isomer: the '(Z)-Tonghaosu' PubChem page returned 404. PubChem CID 5352496 'Tonghaosu' is the (2E) isomer (InChIKey WTRXKCNFPMTAJV-KPKJPENVSA-N, CAS 50257-98-2 / 16863-61-9, MW 200.23), and its synonym list mixes cis/trans labels, so it was NOT used for the cis isomer. Isomeric SMILES not recorded (the NIST page gives only the InChI).

pharmacology.mechanism: Good anti-inflammatory effect in mouse ear inflammation assays; listed among spasmolytic constituents [10].

evidence.claim: Spiroethers are anti-inflammatory in mouse ear models.

compound.teaching_note: A reminder that 'chamomile oil' is not only terpenes: spiroethers are polyacetylenes, typical of the daisy family.
